Package io.mavlink4j.service

Record Class RcChannels

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
io.mavlink4j.service.RcChannels
Record Components:
microsByChannel - one entry per RC channel, 1-based; length 1..16; each entry either within [MIN_MICROS, MAX_MICROS] or equal to RELEASE/IGNORE
public record RcChannels(List<Integer> microsByChannel) extends Record
RC channel override values in microseconds, 1-based (index 0 is channel 1) — the payload ManualControlService relays as a MAVLink RC_CHANNELS_OVERRIDE (#70) frame.

A host application with its own RC-channel type translates to this record at its boundary; the library deliberately depends on nothing of the host's.

Accepts 1..16 channels — MAVLink #70 itself extends to 18, but ArduPilot reads only channels 1..16 (ArduPilot's RC override handling); offering 17/18 would be a lie ManualControlService could never make true. ManualControlService populates every channel a caller supplies, 1..16.

Channels 9..16 do not share 1..8's sentinels on the wire

This record's own RELEASE/IGNORE constants are the domain sentinels — "give this channel back to the RC radio" / "say nothing about this channel" — and mean the same thing regardless of channel number. But MAVLink's own RC_CHANNELS_OVERRIDE spec encodes "release" differently once past channel 8: for channels 1..8, wire 0 is release and wire 65535 is ignore; for channels 9..16, wire 0 or 65535 both mean ignore, and only 65534 (EXTENSION_RELEASE) means release. A caller that reused channels 1..8's RELEASE=0 verbatim on an extension channel would silently send "ignore" instead of "release", leaving that channel latched at its last commanded value forever. wireValue(int) is the one place this asymmetry is resolved, so every other caller in this module can reason about "release" as a single concept.

  • Method Details

    • wireValue

      public int wireValue(int oneBased)
      The value for one RC channel, encoded exactly as MAVLink's own wire format expects for that channel's own range — the one call every frame-builder needs instead of re-deriving the 1..8-vs-9..16 sentinel asymmetry itself (see this record's own class javadoc).
      Parameters:
      oneBased - the RC channel number, 1-based
      Returns:
      IGNORE if oneBased is beyond this frame's own length (a "short" frame pads the rest with ignore); otherwise the channel's stored value, with a domain RELEASE re-encoded as EXTENSION_RELEASE for channel BASE_CHANNEL_COUNT+1 and above
